intent.tagline: A small model asks memory the right question for the main agent.
intent.narration: Past sessions decided many things that a new design should know. Today the agent asks memory only when it thinks to, with its own guess. This plugin gives it a tool that writes better questions and says how far to trust each answer.

problem_solution.problem: The CoBuilder workflows reach Hindsight through one optional build step, and design mode never does. When the main agent queries Hindsight itself, it writes the query from its own guess, and recall returns mostly the chat of the current session.
problem_solution.solution: An opt-in plugin, cobuilder-memory, adds one tool and one command. Haiku reads the person's prompts and the session, writes a recall query, and then picks a knowledge page and writes reflect questions from what recall found. The result says how far to trust each part, and a pane shows the run to the person.
problem_solution.narration: The plugin does not decide what memory means. It asks better questions and hands the answers to the main agent, which checks them against the code.

beats.text: The agent queries memory only when it thinks to, from its own guess, and recall returns mostly the current chat.
ADR-0025 lets only implement ship hooks. A tool, a prompt store, and a pane all need a hook, so ADR-0039 amends the rule for this plugin.
Recall and a page search run first. Haiku then picks a page and writes the reflect questions from the records, so each question names the ADR ids that recall found.
The plugin reaches Hindsight over HTTP, because the MCP server named hindsight differs per repo. Reflect runs through curl, because a fetch stops at 30 seconds.
The agent's replies restate memory, and the Stop hook stores them. The judging rules say a restatement is not newer evidence.

alternatives.option: The 2026-10-13 design: a router, a deep run, and the cc-memory-mirror
alternatives.rejected_because: The spike showed that a plugin cannot start its own subagent. The engineer cut the design to what the spike proved (round 4).
The server named hindsight differs per repo. In think-with-ai it lacked recall and reflect, and one recall result exceeded the MCP result size limit.

alternatives.option: A fixed reflect context in the plugin
alternatives.rejected_because: Fixed text asked reflect to say when memory holds nothing, and the small model overused it. Haiku writes the context from the recall records.

alternatives.option: Run recall and the reflects side by side
alternatives.rejected_because: Reflect questions written before recall cannot name the ADR ids that recall finds. The engineer chose recall first (R1 a).
Reflect links records that recall returns apart. The engineer keeps it, and the main agent judges each answer.

architecture.narration: The plugin is one hooks module beside the session. It stores prompts, answers one tool and one command, calls Haiku twice, calls Hindsight over HTTP, and draws one pane.

beats.text: Plugins meet at the bundle and by name (ADR-0016). Epic E2 names the tool recall_memory, never a plugin path.
The bank comes from the Hindsight config and the main worktree's base name, the same rule the Hindsight runtime uses.
The pane reads one state value that each run step updates, so the person sees the run while the agent waits.
The hooks API is early access, so the plugin tests pin every engine call it makes.
